proposed_fix:
\paragraph{Connection to Assembly Theory.} Our mandatory-assembly claim has a natural affinity with recent work framing life and selection as products of ordered assembly pathways \citep{sharma2023assembly,marshall2021identifying}. Assembly theory quantifies the ``assembly index'' of a molecular structure --- the minimum number of recursive joining operations required to construct it --- and proposes that a high assembly index sustained at high abundance is a signature of selection. We draw this parallel deliberately, but with a caveat: assembly theory is an actively contested framework rather than settled consensus, and several of its stronger claims have attracted substantive published criticism. Empirically, \citet{hazen2024molecular} report that abiotic molecule-like heteropolyanions occurring as precursors to minerals such as ewingite and ilmajokite reach assembly indices as high as 21, so the proposed threshold of $\mathrm{MA} \geq 15$ is not by itself an unambiguous biosignature. Formally, \citet{abrahao2024assembly} argue that the assembly index is equivalent to the size of a minimal context-free grammar and is therefore a Lempel--Ziv-style dictionary compression scheme bounded by Shannon entropy rather than a genuinely new complexity measure, and \citet{uthamacumaran2024salient} report that run-length encoding ($R = 0.900$), Huffman coding ($R = 0.896$) and LZW ($R = 0.874$) track the assembly index closely and match or exceed it as discriminants of living from non-living samples on assembly theory's own datasets. Conceptually, \citet{jaeger2024assembly} argues that the framework detects bias imposed by higher-level constraints in rule-based worlds but does not thereby explain selection or evolution in the Darwinian sense. The assembly-theory authors have replied to the computational-complexity objection \citep{kempes2025assembly}, and the exchange remains open.

We therefore draw the parallel at the level of the shared intuition --- that the \emph{order} in which components are put together carries physical information --- rather than at the level of the disputed formalism. The Trinity ordering articulates an analogous but independent claim at the systems level: the assembly of an autonomous dissipative agent requires a specific sequence of coupled mechanisms, and skipping steps forecloses the process. Critically, our result does not inherit assembly theory's contested premises. We compute no assembly index, infer no selection from molecular abundance, and propose no complexity threshold for life; the ordering reported here is established by direct measurement of transition times across independent simulations and is falsifiable by the laboratory protocols proposed below. Whether the two frameworks can eventually be connected --- whether the Clock $\to$ Map $\to$ Engine sequence corresponds to a minimum assembly path in some assembly-theoretic sense --- remains an open and, in our view, interesting question, but one whose resolution depends on how the current dispute over the assembly index is settled.

proposed_fix: \paragraph{Connection to Assembly Theory.} Our mandatory-assembly claim has a natural affinity with recent work framing life and selection as products of ordered assembly pathways \citep{sharma2023assembly,marshall2021identifying}. Assembly theory quantifies the ``assembly index'' of a molecular structure --- the minimum number of recursive joining operations required to construct it --- and proposes that a high assembly index at high abundance is a signature of selection. We note that this framework is contested rather than settled: its proposed $\mathrm{MA} \geq 15$ biosignature threshold is met by abiotic mineral precursors \citep{hazen2024molecular}, the assembly index has been argued to be equivalent to Lempel--Ziv-style dictionary compression bounded by Shannon entropy and matched or bettered by run-length, Huffman and LZW coding on assembly theory's own data \citep{abrahao2024assembly,uthamacumaran2024salient}, and the claim to \emph{explain} rather than merely quantify selection has been disputed \citep{jaeger2024assembly}; the original authors have replied \citep{kempes2025assembly}. We therefore borrow only the shared intuition that assembly \emph{order} carries physical information. The Trinity ordering articulates an analogous but independent claim at the systems level --- the assembly of an autonomous dissipative agent requires a specific sequence of coupled mechanisms, and skipping steps forecloses the process --- and it invokes no assembly index, no abundance-based inference of selection, and no complexity threshold for life. The tick-to-second conversion is fixed entirely by lipid lateral diffusion; the division period is fixed entirely by lipid accretion and the reduced-volume instability threshold. The two are set by disjoint parts of the model, so the physical division period is a prediction rather than a fit. Converting the measured periods of the \texttt{LIPID\_SUPPLY} ablation (\S5.3) at $0.45\,\mathrm{s}$ per tick gives $T_{\mathrm{div}} = 5{,}101$ ticks $\approx 38$ minutes at baseline supply and $2{,}102$ ticks $\approx 16$ minutes at high supply. An anchor derived from a membrane transport coefficient, applied to a division period derived independently from membrane mechanics, lands in the band where real protocells and real bacteria divide --- which is what one expects if the model's Clock is the same physics that sets real division periods, and a coincidence otherwise.

We state the limits of this plainly. The tick-to-second ratio scales inversely with the assumed lipid diffusion coefficient, which spans an order of magnitude across compositions and temperatures \citep{vaz1984lateral,machan2010lipid}: at $D = 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}^2/\mathrm{s}$ the same $T_{\mathrm{div}}$ maps to roughly $3$ hours, and at $D = 10\,\mu\mathrm{m}^2/\mathrm{s}$ to roughly $19$ minutes. The agreement is therefore an order-of-magnitude concordance, not a calibrated prediction, and it constrains the Clock timescale rather than the reaction-diffusion timescale, which depends on prebiotic chemistry we have not specified. What the anchor establishes is twofold: the predicted Clock-to-Map delay is observable rather than infinitesimal or geological, and the model's division period is not merely dimensionless but falls, unforced, in the band where real cells divide.
